turns.text: hi! need help planning a week of dinners i can actually cook. my current repertoire is scrambled eggs, boxed pasta and one chili recipe. that's it. that's the list. i'd like to get beyond it 🙃

Happy to help. A few quick questions so the plan fits your life: any dietary restrictions or foods you avoid? How much time do you realistically have to cook? And are you cooking for just yourself or for others too?

honestly right now it's takeout or frozen meals nearly every night, so anything homemade is an upgrade. i'm lactose intolerant so no dairy please, i use oat milk. i'm home with my baby son all day so cooking has to fit inside his nap, which is around 12:30. so prep and cooking steps need to fit in that window, and anything that needs longer has to be finished later. cooking for me and my wife, 2 adults

Great, that helps a lot. Since the nap is your window, the trick is to do the hands-on work at 12:30 and let the oven, slow cooker or fridge handle the rest. Here's a dairy-free week that builds on what you already do:

| Day | Dinner | What you do at nap time |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Sheet-pan chicken thighs with potatoes and broccoli | Toss everything in oil, salt, paprika; spread on pan. Roast at dinner time (about 35 min) |
| Tue | Your chili, upgraded with a can of corn and a squeeze of lime | Brown the meat and onions, dump in the rest, let it simmer low |
| Wed | Egg fried rice (a step up from scrambled eggs) | Cook rice and chop veg at nap time; 10 minutes in the pan at dinner |
| Thu | Pasta with olive oil, garlic, cherry tomatoes and white beans | Chop and measure; boil the pasta at dinner. No dairy needed, just skip the parmesan or use nutritional yeast |
| Fri | Slow-cooker salsa chicken tacos | 10 minutes of dumping at nap time; it cooks on its own all afternoon |
| Sat | Leftover chili over baked potatoes | Zero cooking, just reheat |
| Sun | Coconut-milk veggie curry with rice | Chop at nap time; simmer 20 min at dinner |

For anything creamy, oat milk or canned coconut milk works well in place of dairy. Want a shopping list for this?

yes please, in table form. also one thing: i'm not giving up my rare beef pho with no tripe, that's the one takeout i never skip. can you work one night of pho-ish cooking in? or just leave a takeout night open for it

Totally fair. I'd leave Saturday open for your pho run, and move the leftover chili to Monday or Tuesday's lunch instead. If you want a homemade version one night, simple weeknight beef noodle soup is doable, though it won't replace the real thing.

Here's the shopping list:

| Category | Items |
|---|---|
| Protein | Chicken thighs (about 2 lb), ground beef or turkey for chili, eggs, canned white beans |
| Produce | Potatoes, broccoli, onions, garlic, cherry tomatoes, limes, carrots, bell peppers, frozen peas, a veg for the curry (cauliflower or zucchini) |
| Pantry | Rice, pasta, canned tomatoes, kidney beans, canned corn, chili powder, paprika, curry paste, canned coconut milk, soy sauce, olive oil, salsa |
| Other | Tortillas (corn is naturally dairy-free), oat milk, nutritional yeast if you want a cheesy flavor |

Saturday is now open for pho. Start with Monday and Thursday, since they're the easiest wins, and add the rest as you get comfortable.
perfect, thank you. scoreboard: dad 1, takeout 0
Nice start! If a nap runs short, any of these can be paused after the chopping step and finished later. Good luck with the first dinner.
